questions.question: ________ carries oxygenated blood from lungs to heart.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Which type of muscles do the uterus, iris of the eye, and bronchi contain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Smooth muscles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The uterus, iris of the eye, and bronchi contain **smooth muscles**.
 
• **Smooth muscles** are **involuntary, non-striated muscles** found in various internal organs.
 
• These muscles are responsible for various involuntary movements in the body such as the contraction of the uterus during childbirth, adjustment of the iris in response to light, and regulation of airflow in the bronchi.
 
• Unlike skeletal muscles, smooth muscles are not under conscious control and are regulated by the autonomic nervous system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Striated muscles** include **skeletal muscles** that are under voluntary control and are characterized by their striped appearance.
 
• **Skeletal muscles** are attached to bones and help in body movements.
 
• **Cardiac muscles** are specialized **striated muscles found only in the heart**, responsible for pumping blood throughout the body.
 
• Smooth muscles are also found in the walls of blood vessels, digestive tract, and other hollow organs.

questions.question: What is a leaf-shaped ﬂap of cartilage located behind the tongue, at the top of the larynx or voice box called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Epiglottis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The epiglottis is a leaf-shaped flap of cartilage located behind the tongue, at the top of the larynx, or voice box.**

 
 
• The main function of the epiglottis is to seal off the windpipe during eating, so that food is not accidentally inhaled.
 
 
• It stays open during breathing, allowing air into the larynx.
 
 
 
• During swallowing, it closes to prevent aspiration of food into the lungs, forcing the swallowed liquids or food to go along the esophagus toward the stomach instead.
 
• The epiglottis is made of elastic cartilage covered with a mucous membrane, attached to the entrance of the larynx.
 
 
• It projects upwards and backward behind the tongue and the hyoid bone.
 
 
 
• The epiglottis may be inflamed in a condition called epiglottitis, which is most commonly due to the vaccine-preventable bacteria Haemophilus influenzae. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **larynx** is a cartilaginous skeleton, some ligaments, and muscles that move and stabilize it, and a mucous membrane.
 
• The laryngeal skeleton is nine cartilages:
 
 
• the thyroid cartilage, cricoid cartilage, epiglottis, arytenoid cartilages, corniculate cartilages, and cuneiform cartilages.
 
 
 
• The first three are unpaired cartilages, and the latter three are paired cartilages.​

questions.question: Which of the lenses are used to cure Myopia?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **__concave__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Concave lenses** are used to cure **Myopia.**
 
• The term used to explain being short-sighted is **myopia.**
 
• When looking at objects close to them a myopic individual has perfect vision, but distant objects can appear blurred.
 
• This is because, in front of the retina, light is concentrated, and being so far ahead in the eye, objects appear distorted in the distance.
 
• Using a concave (curved inward) lens that is positioned in front of a myopic eye, transferring the vision back to the retina and making it clearer, shortsightedness is corrected.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/251af28b0d9921261646849fffcdbe1dd1366f542497e97d8e21062abbd60de0.png] 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term used to describe being longsighted is **hypermetropia.**
 
• If you are hypermetropic, the image of a surrounding object is generated behind the retina. This indicates that light is focused too far back into the eye causing the appearance of blurred objects nearby.
 
• Using a convex (outward facing) lens,** longsightedness** is corrected. This is situated in front of a hypermetropic eye, pushing the picture forward and correctly focusing it on the retina.
 
• Astigmatism: This defect arises due to the difference in the radius of the curvature of the cornea in the different planes.

 The cylindrical lens is used by people suffering from **Astigmatism**.
 
• Presbyopia arises due to the gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens. It can be cured by using the bi-focal lens of the required power.

questions.question: _______ is the chemical process in which different types of chemical reactions are involved in controlling the living state of the cells in an organism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Metabolism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Metabolism **is the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions in organisms.
 
• It involves various chemical reactions that occur in the cells to maintain the living state of the organism.
 
• These reactions are organized into **metabolic pathways, in which one chemical is transformed through a series of steps into another chemical, by a sequence of enzymes.**
 
• **Metabolism is divided into two categories:** catabolism, the breaking down of compounds to produce** energy; and anabolism, the construction of compounds, which uses energy.**
 
• Metabolism involves the transfer of energy from one form to another, and the conversion of substances into other substances in various metabolic pathways.
 
• The rate of metabolism affects the amount of** food and the type of food that an organism will need; it also affects the physical characteristics of an organism, such as size and shape.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Transportation
 
 
In the context of biology, transportation refers to the movement of substances like nutrients, oxygen, and waste products to and from cells in the body.

 
This can occur through processes such as diffusion, osmosis, or active transport.

 
 
 

 Respiration
 
 
This is the process by which organisms exchange gases with their environment.

 
In cellular respiration, oxygen is used to break down glucose, providing energy in the form of ATP and producing carbon dioxide as a byproduct.

 
 
 

 Excretion
 
 
This is the process by which waste products of metabolism and other non-useful materials are eliminated from an organism.

 
In humans, this primarily occurs via the kidneys, which filter blood and produce urine.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a type of connective tissue?

I. Blood

II. Bone

III. Ligament
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II and III.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Connective tissues** provide** structural support and integrity **to the body, with diverse types such as** loose, dense, adipose, cartilage, bone, and blood,** each contributing unique properties and functions within the extracellular matrix. ***Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.***
 
• The **extracellular matrix,** composed of protein fibres and ground substance, determines the **flexibility, strength, and elasticity of connective tissues,** allowing them to adapt to different mechanical demands.
 
• Apart from their structural roles, connective tissues also play a **crucial role in immunity,** with certain types housing immune cells and contribute to immune responses** against pathogens and foreign substances.**
 
• Connective tissues are essential components of the body, contributing to its **overall architecture, supporting organs and tissues, storing energy, protecting vital structures,** and participating in various **physiological processes.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blood:**

 
 
• Blood is a type of **connective tissue **that consists of cells suspended in a** liquid matrix called plasma.**
 
• It plays a vital role in** transporting oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products** throughout the body.
 
 
 
• **Bone: **
 
 
• Bone is a specialized** connective tissue** that forms the **skeletal structure of the body.**
 
• It provides **support, protection, and facilitates movement. **
 
• Bone tissue is composed of cells called** osteocytes** embedded in a matrix of **collagen fibres and calcium salts.**
 
 
 
• **Ligament: **
 
 
• Ligaments are **fibrous connective tissues** that connect bones to other bones in a joint.
 
• They provide **stability** and help** limit excessive movement **within the joint, contributing to joint strength and function.

questions.question: Triglycerides are a type of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Triglycerides are a type of Fat.**
 
• **Triglycerides:**
 
 
• These are a type of fat (lipid) found in your blood.
 
• It is composed of glycerol and three fatty acids.
 
• Triglycerides and cholesterol are different types of lipids that circulate in the blood.
 
• They store unused calories and provide energy to the body.
 
• Cholesterol is used to build cells and certain hormones.
 
• They are an important measure of heart health.
 
• High triglycerides may contribute to hardening of the arteries or thickening of the artery walls (arteriosclerosis).
 
• It increases the risk of stroke, heart attack, heart disease, and acute inflammation of the pancreas.
 
• Triglycerides fall into a healthy range:
 
 
• **Normal:** Less than 150 milligrams per deciliter (mg/dL), or less than 1.7 millimoles per litre (mmol/L).
 
• **Borderline high:** 150 to 199 mg/dL (1.8 to 2.2 mmol/L).
 
• **High:** 200 to 499 mg/dL (2.3 to 5.6 mmol/L).
 
• **Very high:** 500 mg/dL or above (5.7 mmol/L or above).
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbohydrates:**

 
 
• It is a biomolecule consisting of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms, usually with a hydrogen-oxygen atom ratio of 2:1 and thus with the empirical formula Cm(H2O)n (where m may or may not be different from n).
 
• Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats in foods provide energy for the body's functions and physical activities.
 
• They, however, do not have the same energy content.
 
• The following is the energy- content by respective nutrients:
 
 
• 1 gram of carbohydrates- 4kcal.
 
• 1 gram of protein- 4 kcal.
 
• 1 gram of fats- 9 kcal.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Vitamins:**
 
 
• These are organic compounds that are present in minute amounts in natural foodstuffs.
 
• Most vitamins come from food because the body either does not produce them or produces very little.
 
• Vitamins are of two types.
 
• Fat-soluble vitamins- Vitamins A, D, E, K.
 
• Water-soluble vitamins- Vitamin C and all the B vitamins.
 
 
 
• **Protein:**
 
 
• It plays a role in many body processes:
 
• It maintains proper fluid regulation and fluid balance.
 
• It is helpful in immune system responses.
 
• Protein helps in growth and maintenance.
 
• Aids in biochemical reactions.
 
• They serve as hormones and messengers.
 
• It helps in maintaining proper pH.
 
• It supplies the body with energy.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of the substance that forms the tooth enamel in the human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium hydroxyapatite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Calcium hydroxyapatite (Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2)** is the primary mineral that forms the hard, protective outer layer of human teeth known as enamel.
 
• Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body, and its durability is due to the crystalline structure of calcium hydroxyapatite.
 
• This mineral provides strength and resilience to teeth, enabling them to withstand the forces of chewing and grinding.
 
• Calcium hydroxyapatite also plays a role in maintaining the natural whiteness and smooth surface of enamel, which is critical for oral health.
 
• The presence of fluoride in dental products helps to convert hydroxyapatite into fluorapatite, which is more resistant to acid attacks from bacteria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tooth Enamel:**

 
 
• Tooth enamel is made up of 96% minerals, primarily calcium hydroxyapatite, with the remainder being water and organic matter.
 
• It is non-living tissue, which means it cannot regenerate or repair itself once damaged.
 
• Enamel erosion can occur due to exposure to acids from foods, drinks, or bacterial activity, leading to tooth sensitivity and cavities.
 
 
 
• **Hydroxyapatite in Bones:**
 
 
• Calcium hydroxyapatite is also a major component of bones, providing them with strength and structure.
 
• In bones, hydroxyapatite is embedded in a matrix of collagen, making them both strong and flexible.
 
 
 
• **Role of Fluoride:**
 
 
• Fluoride strengthens tooth enamel by forming fluorapatite, which is more resistant to decay.
 
• Fluoride is commonly added to toothpaste and drinking water to promote dental health.
 
 
 
• **Dental Health Practices:**
 
 
• Maintaining good oral hygiene, such as regular brushing and flossing, helps prevent enamel erosion and decay.
 
• Avoiding excessive consumption of acidic foods and drinks can protect enamel from damage.

questions.question: Which of the following hormone is secreted by brain that helps to regulate sleep-wake cycles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Melatonin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Melatonin hormone is secreted by the brain that helps to regulate sleep-wake cycles**.
 
• **Melatonin** is a hormone primarily released by the pineal gland at night and has long been associated with control of the sleep-wake cycle.
 
 
• As a dietary supplement, it is often used for the short-term treatment of insomnia, such as from jet lag or shift work, and is typically taken orally.
 
• Evidence of its benefit for this use, however, is not strong.
 
• A 2017 review found that sleep onset occurred six minutes faster with use, but found no change in total time asleep.
 
• Side effects from melatonin supplements are minimal at low doses for short durations.
 
• Melatonin side effects are rare but may occur in 1 to 10 patients in 1000.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxytocin** is a hormone that acts on organs in the body (including the breast and uterus) and as a chemical messenger in the brain, controlling key aspects of the reproductive system, including childbirth and lactation, and aspects of human behaviour.
 
• **Insulin** is a peptide hormone produced by beta cells of the pancreatic islets.
 
 
• It is considered to be the main anabolic hormone of the body.
 
• It regulates the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats, and protein by promoting the absorption of glucose from the blood into the liver, fat, and skeletal muscle cells.
 
 
 
• **Aldosterone** is the main mineralocorticoid steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.
 
 
• It is essential for sodium conservation in the kidney, salivary glands, sweat glands, and colon.

questions.question: Irregular growth of teeth is due to the deficiencies of vitamin ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vitamin D** plays a crucial role in calcium absorption and bone health, which is essential for proper dental growth and alignment.
 
• Deficiency of Vitamin D can lead to improper mineralization of teeth, causing irregular growth and dental deformities.
 
• Conditions such as **rickets** (in children) and **osteomalacia** (in adults) due to Vitamin D deficiency can affect jawbone development and tooth alignment.
 
• Sources of Vitamin D include exposure to sunlight, fortified foods, fatty fish, and dietary supplements.
 
• Proper intake of Vitamin D is especially important during childhood, as it is a critical period for dental and skeletal development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rickets:** A condition caused by Vitamin D deficiency in children leading to weak or soft bones, dental issues, and skeletal deformities.
 
• **Osteomalacia:** Softening of bones in adults due to poor bone mineralization, often linked with Vitamin D deficiency.
 
• **Calcium and Vitamin D:** Both nutrients work in synergy; Vitamin D enhances calcium absorption in the intestines, necessary for strong teeth and bones.
 
• **Hypervitaminosis D:** Excessive Vitamin D intake can lead to toxicity, causing hypercalcemia (high calcium levels) and affecting overall health.
 
• **Sunlight Exposure:** The body synthesizes Vitamin D naturally when skin is exposed to sunlight; however, factors like pollution, sunscreen, and lifestyle can limit this process.

questions.question: Which cell found in the bone marrow acts as a repair system for the body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stem cells**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stem cells** are found in the **bone marrow** and **act as a repair system for the body**.
 
• These cells have the unique ability to develop into different types of cells in the body, including** bone cells, fat cells, and muscle cells**.
 
• Stem cells play a crucial role in the body's ability to heal and regenerate tissues.
 
• They can divide and produce new stem cells (self-renewal) or differentiate into specialized cells (differentiation).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bone marrow** is a spongy tissue found in the center of bones, particularly in the hip and thigh bones.
 
• It is responsible for producing blood cells, including red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, through a process called **hematopoiesis**.
 
• There are two types of stem cells found in the bone marrow: **hematopoietic stem cells** (which give rise to blood cells) and **mesenchymal stem cells** (which can develop into bone, cartilage, and fat cells).
 
• Stem cell research holds significant potential for developing treatments for various diseases and injuries, including leukemia, lymphoma, and spinal cord injuries.

• Pivot joints, also known as rotary joints,
 
• Pivot joints permit axial rotation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• There are only two ball and socket joints in human body – one in the shoulder and the other in the hip
 
 
 
• The hinge joint is commonly referred to as the knee.__
 
 
• Hinge Joint is a joint in the human body that serves motion in one plane.
 
• It is a common class of synovial joint that includes the:-
 
• Ankle
 
• Knee
 
• Finger Joints 
 
• Toe Joints​

• There are some bones in our head that are joined together at some joints. The bones cannot move at these joints. Such joints are called fixed joints.
